author: Erick Tay
description: More secrets, details, and analysis of the almost every official GTA 6 screenshots available.
title: We Analyzed Every Official GTA 6 Screenshot Continued

author: Mark Delaney
description:
Being obsessed with zombie fiction for as long as I have been, I'm comfortable saying No More Room in Hell 2 is the year's best zombie game. Since I first played it in early access two years ago, I've loved its Romero-inspired vibes and slower, more punishing take on a Left 4 Dead-style game--doubling the co-op team size to eight players is a fun wrinkle, too. 

So imagine my surprise when I recently hopped back into the game and found its latest update added a map that goes in a much different direction, trading its Night of the Living Dead inspirations for something much more at home in Friday the 13th.

The Camp Blood update brings a slasher-inspired summer-camp map, Ruby Lake, to the game's wave-based Survival mode, which lives alongside its more campaign-like Scenario mode. Not
title: The Best Zombie Game Of 2026 Just Went From George Romero To Jason Voorhees

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Electronic Arts recently killed off Mass Effect and closed developer BioWare entirely, but the publisher is still trying to make money from the franchise's fanbase.

Ahead of the annual Mass Effect holiday of N7 Day on November 7, EA is promoting Mass Effect via posts about what fans can buy on the BioWare Gear Store. A lot of people online are saying this is tone deaf and gross behavior.

The BioWare Gear Store's social media presence came back to life after a month of darkness today to start hawking Mass Effect merch. The post that kicked things off is the one below, in which fans are invited to "celebrate the legacy" of Mass Effect by giving EA money.

EA followed the post up with eight more, pushing people to visit the BioWare Gear Store to buy things like mugs, tote bags, clothing, and shoes, among other things.
title: EA Killed Mass Effect But Is Still Trying To Make Money On It

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
If you're among the millions of Amazon Prime subscribers--maybe you use the platform to buy games--you're getting a new perk in the form of free delivery with Uber Eats.

Amazon and Uber today announced a partnership where US Prime subscribers can get free delivery on orders of $25 or more. Orders can be placed on Amazon's website or through the app, as opposed to the Uber Eats app.

The benefit works for Prime members in the US, including the cheaper Prime for Young Adults and Prime Access membership tiers. Additionally, Uber Eats is offering $20 off each of your first two orders of $25 or more through November 18.

With this added perk, you can order some wings
title: Buy Games On Prime? Your Membership Now Gets You Free Uber Eats Delivery, Too

author: Ben Janca
description: While on the surface, Stellar Blade on Switch 2 seems like another successful port to Nintendo’s latest handheld, it has a few important tradeoffs that ultimately make it difficult to recommend, even with the fantastic benefit of getting to play it on the go.
title: Stellar Blade On Switch 2 Has One Fatal Flaw

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
As part of Nintendo's latest earnings briefing, the company said it has no plans to increase the Switch 2 price again, or at least not anytime soon.

VGC reported that management said Nintendo has enough memory stockpiled to shield itself and thus not need to implement another price hike.

Nintendo raised the price of the Switch 2 in September, bringing it up from $450 to $500. This followed price hikes for the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S consoles, meaning that all three major platforms have seen hikes.
title: Switch 2 Won’t Get Another Price Hike, At Least Not Soon, Nintendo Says

author: Ben Janca
description: We go through all of the main dungeon bosses in the child and adult era, using no HUD and taking no damage through the entire run.
title: All Dungeon Bosses No Damage – Ocarina Of Time Remake

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description: Compared to previous games in the series, Grand Theft Auto 6 looks like it'll only be a few steps removed from reality when it launches this month. Actions have consequences, working on a relationship requires more than just hitting a few button prompts, and bulking up means that you'll have to visit an in-game gym regularly. Will all of that add up to an experience that can give a little dude in green a run for his money as the best-reviewed game of the year? Who knows, but what I do know is that Rockstar Games better have some hygiene options in the game, becau
title: GTA 6 Looks Pretty Realistic, Until It Comes To Gym Etiquette

author: Steve Watts
description:
The Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is a true showpiece for the Switch 2, and one of the best-looking games on the system. It's also, for lots of older players who remember the original Ocarina of Time, a deeply nostalgic experience, so a lot of the joy comes down to seeing familiar moments reenvisioned with this beautiful presentation. As a result, I've been hammering my screenshot button like never before, all throughout the review experience.

Now to be clear, I'm not someone who often uses the screenshot button at all. I think I've touched it a half-dozen times, tops, since the Switch 2 came out. Occasionally I use it for note-keeping or other work purposes, but I hardly ever think to take a screenshot on my own simply because I'm wowed by something. That's what made my use of it in Ocarina so surprising to me. I just kept hitting cinematic sequences, boss fights, or other visual treats that I felt compelled to make a
title: The Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Wore Out My Screenshot Button

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Rockstar has released a big batch of new Grand Theft Auto 6 screenshots as part of what the developer is calling a "launch gallery."

The brand-new images show off main characters Jason and Lucia in a variety of settings, including a nightclub, the dive bar The Rusty Anchor, and the gym, where Jason is putting in some work on the bench.
title: GTA 6: Lots Of New Images Have Been Released

author: Steve Watts
description:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2 is very faithful, but it also takes some liberties and notable updates. From our wide-ranging interview with producers Eiji Aonuma and Hidemaro Fujibayashi, it sounds like this was something of a training ground for younger staffers to understand the world and dungeon design of a classic Zelda format, but they also weren't too beholden to the original design. In fact, Aonuma said he would push back against young developers who defaulted to the original design.

In response to a question about dungeon design, Fujibayashi said the senior staff would play "memory erasure" exercises, pretending that this is their first time seeing a dungeon to approach it with fresh eyes. Even though they know the solutions, they would act a if they don'
title: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time’s Aonuma Says He Always Rejected This Excuse

author: Chris Compendio
description:
As the fate of Arkane Lyon hangs in the balance, a union representing workers from the French studio offered strong words toward Arkane's parent company, Microsoft. In short, the union blames Microsoft for "sabotaging" the production of its Blade game.

French trade union STJV (per VGC) claimed that development on Marvel's Blade is "going fine," but said that workers face the "harsh reality" that Microsoft may close the studio for financial reasons. But the union said that the onus for Arkane's tough financial situation is on Microsoft itself, claiming that a hiring freeze that lasted 19 months "artificially caused delay and additional cost."

STJV asserts that closing Ar
title: Arkane Union Accuses Microsoft Of “Sabotaging” Development Of Marvel’s Blade

author: Callum Self
description:
There’s one point in Phantom Blade Zero where you, playing as the impressive swordsman Soul, walk onto a bridge. A man, stumbling around without a care in the world, starts to speak with you. He’s clearly drunk and eventually pulls his sword free. That man is Hua Qianxiao, and despite being fairly early into the game, the encounter demonstrated how challenging things would be--the first boss was just an appetizer for what the new action RPG would deliver. Despite some heavy hitters this year, it might be a top contender for my Game of the Year, and you could play it for a fraction of the price.

Now, don’t get me wrong, the story is fine—it’s serviceable and drives the narrative—but what makes Phantom Blade Zero one of the top action games of the year is, well, the action. Described by developer S-Game as "kung-fu punk,"
title: Phantom Blade Zero Has Won Me Over As A Game Of The Year Candidate, And You Could Get It For $1

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
Marvel's Wolverine got off to a strong start when it launched in September, but since then, it looks like things have cooled off massively for the game. In its new earnings report, Sony finally dropped a sales number for Insomniac's new Marvel game, revealing that it has sold 2.4 million units so far.

Marvel's Wolverine, as it initially debuted as September's best-selling game, delivering the highest launch-month dollar sales for a Sony-published game si
title: Marvel’s Wolverine Has Lost Its Momentum, And Sony’s Numbers Show It

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Grand Theft Auto 6 is the biggest game that Rockstar Games has ever made, and it was no doubt very expensive to produce. But just how much did it cost? We know it's not $1.5 billion, but Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick has now reacted to the discussion around the game's development costs.

He told The Wall S
title: GTA 6 Boss Talks The Game’s Budget And Calls Out A “High-Profile” Game For Releasing In A Rough State

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
Since its launch last year, the Switch 2 has proven itself to be a portable powerhouse, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake may just be the best game to show off its capabilities. The upgraded version of the timeless adventure looks even better when compared to the original N64 game that first debuted in 1998, as Nintendo has leveraged the Switch 2 hardware to create the definitive version of the game, blending atmospheric design with imaginatively designed character models.

And if you want to see just how gorgeous that glow-up is, click the video below for a guided tour of Hyrule across two eras of Nintendo hardware. No commentary, just comparisons.
title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time’s 2026 Remake Looks Stunning Next To The Original N64 Game

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description: There's no shortage of dedicated video capture devices on the market, but if you're looking for something that cuts down on cable clutter and adds some cyberpunk vibes to your setup, you'll want to check out the Chizha Mount Ling 2 Pro. GameSpot recently went hands-on with it, and while it's a great capture device for PC handhelds like the Steam Deck and the Asus ROG Xbox Ally X, it's hard to recommend if you're planning to grab Switch 2 footage specifically.
title: This Handheld Gaming Hub Has A Lot More Going On Than You’d Expect

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
With the PS5 entering its sixth year of active duty later this month, it looks like development on the yet-to-be-announced PS6 is picking up speed. During a briefing on its latest financial results, Sony said that research and development was proceeding smoothly on its "next-generation" platform.

"Looking ahead to the next fiscal year, we aim to continue to enhance user engagement and further strengthen monetization through the release of strong titles and the expansion of our service. We also intend to make solid progress in preparing for the next-generation platform," Sony CFO Lin Tao said (via
title: Sony Is Getting Serious About The PS6, But Don’t Expect An Announcement Just Yet

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
During a briefing on its latest financial results, Sony revealed it sold 2.6 million PS5 consoles in its last quarter, which ended on September 30. This brings lifetime PS5 sales to 97.9 million, just months before the console enters its sixth year on the market. By comparison, the PS4 had shipped 103.0 million units at the same point in its lifecycle, but Sony's gaming ecosystem is performing much better thanks to higher digital revenue and a massive active user base.

This comes at a time when the PS5 has only gotten more expensive since launch, thanks to the global components shortage that has seen memory prices surge. Sony says it has been in discussions with manufacturers to secure enough memory for the next fiscal year and expects its hardware sales to remain profitable into the
title: PS5 Is Closing In On 100 Million Sales, Despite Getting More Expensive

author: Gabe Gurwin
description:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has been regarded as one of the best games ever made for nearly 30 years, and its new Switch 2 remake is seeing similar levels of acclaim. Part of the reason for its critical success seems to be its deep understanding of the source material, and that shouldn't be a surprise when considering how well Nintendo has retained staff over the years--something very few other game companies have managed to do.

Speaking to GameSpot, longtime Zelda producer Eiji Aonuma acknowledged the benefits of having developers on the team who have been working at Nintendo for decades.

"I think you see a real benefit to having some very long-term-tenured staff members around who have shared the same experiences over time, because every time you get to the next step, it's easier to discuss how to proceed, or if you're going to do something new," Aonuma said via an inter
title: How Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Benefits From A Glaringly Obvious Tactic That Few Game Devs Follow

author: Steve Watts
description:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is one of Nintendo's most revered games of all time, even by the lofty standards of a company known for making influential, groundbreaking video games. That legacy means extra care and consideration put into remaking the game for modern audiences on the Nintendo Switch 2, with a remake that is receiving a glowing reception both in our GameSpot review and across the industry. It is now the top-ranked game of 2026 on GameSpot sister site Metacritic.

It's a titanic achievement, but to hear producers Eiji Aonuma and Hidemaro Fujibayashi, it was also intended as a learning experience for both the new generation, and for t
title: Nintendo Explains How It Made The Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Only It Could Create

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
Remaking a game like The Legend of Zelda: The Ocarina of Time required Nintendo to nail a fine balance between staying faithful to the original and updating it where it mattered. The Ocarina of Time remake largely sticks to the original's foundations while adding features like a dedicated jump button and updated controls. That was one of several changes, as Nintendo's core design philosophy was to modernize execution and comfort while preserving the original emotional and narrative intent.

As Legend of Zelda producer Hidemaro Fujibayashi explained in an interview with GameSpot, early pre-production focused on setting clear boundaries for what would and wouldn't change in the remake. "One of the first discussions we had leading up to the full-blown development of the title was really clearly establishing what it is we were going to ch
title: Nintendo Wanted Ocarina Of Time To Feel Better In The Remake, Not Just Different

author: Ben Janca
description:
Enjoy this graphics comparison of the original N64 version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and the brand new Switch 2 remake.

This video will cover from the beginning of the game up to getting the Master Sword.

Footage of the N64 version is captured from an original NTSC 1.0 cartridge running on an Analogue 3D with de-blur enabled.
title: Ocarina of Time – Original vs Remake Comparison

author: Steve Watts
description:
Every The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time player remembers their first encounter with the ReDeads. The shambling zombie-like enemies occupy Hyrule Castle Town when you emerge from the Temple of Time and immediately freak you out, with a sudden piercing scream that freezes you in place. The new ReDeads work largely the same way, but at one point in development they were made significantly scarier.

"With this remake, the graphics are a lot improved, and so the ReDead--the sound, the graphics, and the movement--ended up being very, very scary," producer Hidemaro Fujibayashi told GameSpot via a translator. "And the staff wanted to make this in service of making a good gameplay experience. But from our perspective, taking a step back, we felt like, let's remember the experience that we don't want to change, and taking that into consideration, maybe we've gone a step too far, so let's dial it back."
title: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Accidentally Made ReDeads Too Scary At One Point

author: Steve Watts
description:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2 is a mostly faithful remake, but it does introduce some new features and bells and whistles that modernize the experience. Some of those are very noticeable, like the addition of a jump button, while others are more subtle. One such subtle change is the new full-day passage of time inside Hyrule Castle Town, which also means NPCs need something to do all night. And according to producer Hidemaro Fujibayashi, that meant a ton of extra work, especially for him.

"I reviewed every single text of the NPCs," Fujibayashi told GameSpot. "And befo
title: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time’s NPCs Stay Busy All Night, And Sounds Like That Was A Pain

author: Cameron Koch
description:
World of Warcraft: Forever's launch hit some minor hiccups immediately upon release, but overall is going surprisingly well, much to the surprise of players who anticipated the worst.

As soon as the countdown timer clicked to zero at 3 PM PT, players began to encounter short login queues. Sitting through the queue would bring up the game's list of possible rulesets, but they were grayed out an unavailable. It took around 30 minutes of players requeuing and waiting with bated breath to see if the servers would come online or if they were out of luck, but lo and behold, eventually everything started working as intended.
title: WoW: Forever’s Launch Is Going Surprisingly Smooth
